subtype: Approach: using the caregiver as a tool [Action]
passage: In the flat's living room Ayesha stopped facing the sofa, lifted both arms high and said "Up." Charu, Ayesha's father, put down the newspaper, scooped Ayesha under the arms and set the toddler on the seat. Ayesha wriggled into the corner with a soft "Ah," and picked up the cushion. No climbing was needed at all.

qa.q: What word did Ayesha say in front of the sofa?
What was Ayesha feeling with both arms raised at the sofa?
qa.a: Ayesha was trusting and expectant, sure Charu would do the lifting, and content once seated.

qa.q: What could Ayesha try in place of asking, and why?
qa.a: Ayesha could try hooking a knee onto the cushion edge first, with Charu close, because trying helps the legs learn a skill that lifting does not teach.

qa.q: How might Charu see this way of getting onto the sofa?
qa.a: Charu finds it quick and easy to lift Ayesha, and probably enjoys being asked, but may want to give a chance to climb sometimes.

grounding: A toddler lifts both arms and says "up" and the father lifts the toddler onto the sofa, so no climbing is needed.
